fair_value.method: Horizon-date (Sep-2027) value for Ero Copper, blending forward EV/EBITDA (~$38, weight 0.5), 2028E P/E (~$38, 0.3) and a conservative long-term-copper DCF/NAV (~$30, 0.2). Near-term deck raised to ~$5.90/lb realized (was $5.75), gold $3,800/oz, ~82kt NTM Cu at C1 ~$2.28/lb, ~106M diluted shares, ~$150M horizon net debt.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM-at-horizon (Q4-27 to Q3-28) EBITDA ~$695M: ~82kt Cu (180.8M lb) x ($5.90 realized - $2.28 C1) = $654M, plus ~55koz Au x ($3,800 - $1,250 C1) = $140M, less ~$100M G&A/exploration/royalties/other. x 6.0x (peer/historical 5-7x) = EV $4.17B, less ~$150M horizon net debt (Q2-26 $452.7M; 2027 FCF ~$300M) = $4.02B / 106M = ~$38.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E (first full Pilar-shaft year, 80-90kt filed outlook): EBITDA ~$720M at $5.90 Cu / 86kt, less D&A ~$170M, interest ~$30M, tax ~22% -> NI ~$405M / 106M = EPS ~$3.80 x 10x = $38. (Round 1 used $4.75 x 8x; EPS base lowered to match a bottom-up D&A/tax build, multiple raised to a producer norm.)

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Normalized post-2027 FCF ~$350M/yr at long-term Cu ~$5.00-5.25/lb, 15-year life, 10% discount rate -> ~$2.66B; plus risked Furnas 60% interest ~$0.4B (PEA NPV8 $2.0B is 100%-basis at $4.60 Cu, ~$1.2B attributable before Vale carry; PEA stage, PFS 2027, FID 2029); less ~$0.35B net debt today -> ~$2.7B / 106M ~ $26 today, rolled forward one year with deleveraging ~$29-30. Consistent with peers at ~0.85-0.95x NAV on $4.00-4.50 decks. Weight cut from 0.3 to 0.2 to avoid double-counting copper mean reversion.

bear.story: Copper retraces to ~$4.75-5.00/lb realized (below Citi's ~$5.44 2027 base) as the US tariff/stockpiling premium unwinds and supply disruptions heal; Pilar shaft transition slips so 2028 uplift moves out; 2027 guidance set at the low end of 75-85kt with C1 above $2.40 (Q2-26 ran $2.42 vs $2.15-2.35 guide). EBITDA ~$500M x 4.5-5x, net debt ~$250M -> ~$22-24.

base.story: Realized copper ~$5.75-6.25/lb (between Citi and Goldman's $6.26 2027 view, below LME spot); 2026 guidance roughly met, 2027 guided within 75-85kt, capex steps down, net debt ~$100-200M by Sep-2027 and a first capital-return plan; shaft reaches bottom and transitions to operation for full 2028 benefit. ~6x NTM EBITDA -> ~$38.

bull.story: Copper deficit persists (Goldman sees ex-US deficits in 2026-27), realized $6.50+/lb; Tucuma hits 4 Mtpa run-rate on filtration upgrades, shaft on time, Furnas PFS shows a large high-grade project; net cash by late 2027 plus buybacks/dividend drive 7x NTM EBITDA of ~$850M+ -> mid-$50s.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$22 (-42%) the equity (~$2.3B) plus ~$200-300M net debt would be ~3.7x 2027 EBITDA even at $5.00/lb copper (~$560M at 77kt, C1 $2.30). Getting there requires copper sustained below ~$4.75/lb (under every current bank 2027 forecast) or a company-specific failure: Pilar shaft slipping past 2027, Tucuma filtration not lifting throughput, 2027 guidance well below the filed 75-85kt, or re-leveraging. BRL collars (floor 5.40) through Dec-2027 limit the FX cost channel, so a post-election BRL rally alone should not get it there. Kept slightly below the supervisor's $23 because 50%+ vol makes a -40% print from a copper wobble plausible without fundamental damage.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor established with filed evidence that (a) Goldman's 2027 LME average is $13,800/t (~$6.26/lb, raised 1 Jun 2026; I verified), Citi ~$5.44, LME spot ~$6.5-6.6, and Ero realized $5.78 in Q2-26 (verified in the Q2 MD&A); (b) $450M USD/BRL collars (floor 5.40, cap 6.34) run to Dec-2027 (verified); (c) horizon net debt ~$100-200M is right; (d) Furnas PEA NPV is 100%-basis; (e) Q3 results come in early November, not October. Its main critique of me - a below-bank near-term deck plus a 30% long-term DCF weight double-counts copper mean reversion - is fair. I fixed it partly on each side: near-term realized deck up to ~$5.90 (not the full $6.00, because Ero's realized price has run below LME and costs are tracking above guidance: YTD C1 $2.40 vs $2.15-2.35), and DCF weight cut to 0.2. I also rebuilt the P/E leg bottom-up (2028E EPS ~$3.80 x 10x rather than $4.75 x 8x; same $38). Blend 0.5x38 + 0.3x38 + 0.2x30 = ~$36.5 (from $35), a touch below the supervisor's $37.5 for the realized-price and cost reasons. CMD commentary (via Quartr/search) confirms 2027 is a shaft-transition year with full benefit in 2028 and no new filed multi-year guidance. Scenarios $23/$38/$56 at 25/50/25 give a mean ~$38.8 and median ~$37. Ladder: lognormal median raised from $36.5 to ~$37.0, sigma 0.50 (below 64% trailing vol, which included a rerating, but far above large-cap 25-35% given single-commodity, Brazil and single-shaft risk), with the far-left tail slightly fattened for a copper crash and far-right slightly trimmed. Research limited to web sources; no options data used.
